HDAC1 regulates invasion and HDAC6 regulates migration in ccRCC and both are regulated by HIF-2a and ERa, respectively.

The main takeaway from our work is that
HDAC1 is a transcriptional target of HIFs and that it promotes invasion and migration of ccRCC cell lines.
HDAC1 is regulated by hypoxia and HIF-2, and that it promotes invasiveness by regulating the expression of MMPs, while HDAC6 promotes cell migration by decreasing acetylation of α-tubulin.
HDAC1 may be a potential target to reduce ccRCC invasiveness and that HDAC6 may be a target to reduce ccRC cell migration.
